fuente.nota: Texto recortado por párrafos; sin cambios en las frases.

parrafos: Ukraine and the United States reached a deal on April 30 to give the US preferential access to new Ukrainian rare earth mineral deals and to create a new fund to attract investors and help in rebuilding war-torn Ukraine. It was signed in Washington by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent for the US and First Vice Prime Minister Yulia Svyrydenko for Ukraine.

US President Donald Trump proposed the agreement, publicly stating that he expects something in return for military aid to Ukraine. It would give the US priority in new Ukrainian investments to mine 55 minerals – these include lithium, titanium, lanthanum, uranium, and cerium, among other rare earth and precious minerals.

The accord did not include debt obligations for Ukraine, – previously proposed, but rejected by Ukraine – and Kyiv would still decide what to mine and where. It also does not provide the US access to operations the Ukrainian side already profits from.

The Ukrainian side would be expected to deposit 50% of its future profits from government-owned resources listed above, while the US would help via monetary and military aid. No profits would be taken from the Fund for ten years.

The current version, establishing the so-called United States–Ukraine Reinvestment Fund, was reached after intense negotiations; a previous iteration – later derided by the Ukrainian side – was almost signed before a now-famous altercation between US President Donald Trump and his Ukrainian counterpart, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, devolved into Zelenskyy being told to leave the White House.

The signing was praised publicly by both sides – it "clearly signals the Trump Administration's commitment to a free, sovereign, prosperous Ukraine" – the White House said. "Importantly, the Agreement sends a signal to global partners that long-term cooperation with Ukraine – over decades – is not only possible but reliable," Svyrydenko posted on the social media platform X.

Former president and prime minister under Vladimir Putin, now the deputy chairman of the Security Council of Russia, Dmitry Medvedev stated: "Trump has broken the Kyiv regime into paying for American aid with minerals. Now they will have to pay for military supplies with the national wealth of a disappearing country."
titulo_es: Ucrania y EE. UU. alcanzan un acuerdo sobre minerales
resumen_es: Ucrania y Estados Unidos firman un acuerdo que da a EE. UU. acceso preferente a futuros proyectos de minerales ucranianos y crea un fondo de inversión para la reconstrucción. La noticia explica sus condiciones, el difícil proceso negociador y las reacciones de Washington, Kiev y Moscú.
nivel_motivo: Texto breve y de estructura sencilla; el vocabulario difícil (iteration, derided, altercation) es limitado y se deduce del contexto.

ideas_clave.idea: On 30 April Washington and Kyiv signed an agreement granting the US privileged access to future Ukrainian mineral projects and setting up a fund to attract investment for post-war reconstruction.
The deal was promoted by Trump as a way of obtaining something in exchange for military support and covers some 55 minerals, including lithium, titanium and uranium.

Ukraine takes on no debt and keeps control over mining decisions; it will pay half of the future profits from state-owned resources into the fund, the US will contribute aid, and nothing can be withdrawn for a decade.
The final text emerged from tough negotiations after an earlier draft collapsed following a public clash between Trump and Zelenskyy at the White House.
Both signatories hailed the deal as proof of long-term commitment, whereas Russia's Medvedev mocked it as Ukraine paying for weapons with its national wealth.

resumen_modelo: The article reports that on 30 April Ukraine and the United States signed a deal giving Washington priority access to new investments in 55 Ukrainian minerals and creating a joint fund for reconstruction. Promoted by Trump as compensation for military aid, the final version imposes no debt on Kyiv, which keeps control over mining; Ukraine will contribute half of its future profits from state resources, while the US will provide aid. Although both governments hailed the accord, reached after a stormy earlier attempt, Russia's Medvedev mocked it as paying for weapons with national wealth.

preguntas.enunciado: Indica si la afirmación es verdadera (V), falsa (F) o no se dice (ND).
preguntas.pregunta: The agreement was signed in Kyiv by the US Treasury Secretary and Ukraine's First Vice Prime Minister.
preguntas.cita: It was signed in Washington by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent for the US and First Vice Prime Minister Yulia Svyrydenko for Ukraine.
preguntas.explicacion: Los firmantes son correctos, pero el acuerdo se firmó en Washington, no en Kiev.

preguntas.pregunta: How many minerals does the agreement cover?
preguntas.cita: It would give the US priority in new Ukrainian investments to mine 55 minerals
preguntas.explicacion: El texto habla de 55 minerales. El 50 es el porcentaje de beneficios y el 10 el número de años sin retiradas del fondo.

preguntas.enunciado: Indica si la afirmación es verdadera (V), falsa (F) o no se dice (ND).
preguntas.pregunta: Trump openly linked the agreement to the military aid the US had given Ukraine.
preguntas.cita: publicly stating that he expects something in return for military aid to Ukraine
preguntas.explicacion: Trump declaró públicamente que esperaba una contrapartida por la ayuda militar, así que la afirmación es verdadera.

preguntas.enunciado: Indica si la afirmación es verdadera (V), falsa (F) o no se dice (ND).
preguntas.pregunta: Under the final agreement, Ukraine must repay part of the aid as debt.
preguntas.cita: The accord did not include debt obligations for Ukraine
preguntas.explicacion: Las obligaciones de deuda se propusieron en una versión anterior, pero Ucrania las rechazó y no figuran en el acuerdo final.

preguntas.pregunta: Who decides which resources are mined and where?
preguntas.cita: Kyiv would still decide what to mine and where
preguntas.explicacion: «Kyiv» se usa como metonimia del Gobierno ucraniano, que conserva la decisión. El texto no menciona ningún comité conjunto ni el papel de los inversores en esa decisión.

preguntas.pregunta: What will Ukraine contribute to the fund?
opciones: Half of its future profits from state-owned resources
All of its current mining revenues
Half of the profits of its private mining companies
A fixed annual payment for ten years
respuestas: Half of its future profits from state-owned resources
preguntas.cita: The Ukrainian side would be expected to deposit 50% of its future profits from government-owned resources listed above
preguntas.explicacion: Se trata del 50 % de los beneficios futuros de recursos públicos. El párrafo 2 aclara que las explotaciones actuales quedan fuera, y no se habla de empresas privadas ni de pagos fijos.

preguntas.enunciado: Busca en el párrafo 0 una expresión que signifique «devastado por la guerra».
preguntas.pregunta: Find an expression meaning 'devastated by war'.
preguntas.explicacion: «War-torn» (literalmente «desgarrado por la guerra») es la colocación habitual para un país arrasado por un conflicto.

preguntas.enunciado: Busca en el párrafo 4 una palabra que signifique «ridiculizada, despreciada».
preguntas.pregunta: Find a word meaning 'mocked, treated with contempt'.
preguntas.cita: a previous iteration – later derided by the Ukrainian side – was almost signed
preguntas.explicacion: «To deride» es burlarse de algo o despreciarlo; la parte ucraniana criticó con dureza la versión anterior.

preguntas.enunciado: Indica si la afirmación es verdadera (V), falsa (F) o no se dice (ND).
preguntas.pregunta: The new fund will be managed by the World Bank.
preguntas.explicacion: El texto da el nombre del fondo (United States–Ukraine Reinvestment Fund), pero no dice quién lo gestionará.

preguntas.pregunta: What does the ten-year rule on profits suggest about the purpose of the fund?
respuestas: It suggests that the fund is designed to reinvest in Ukraine's reconstruction over the long term rather than to provide immediate returns to the United States.
preguntas.cita: No profits would be taken from the Fund for ten years.
preguntas.explicacion: Es una inferencia: si no se retiran beneficios en diez años, el dinero se queda invertido en Ucrania. Encaja con el nombre de «Reinvestment Fund».

preguntas.pregunta: How does Medvedev's view of the deal differ from that of the signatories?
respuestas: While the White House and Kyiv present it as a sign of long-term commitment and reliable cooperation, Medvedev portrays it as Ukraine being forced to pay for US weapons with its national resources.
preguntas.cita: Trump has broken the Kyiv regime into paying for American aid with minerals.
preguntas.explicacion: Hay que contraponer la lectura positiva de los firmantes (párrafo 5) con la interpretación de Medvedev, que lo presenta como una forma de expolio.
